The issue requested setting the `disabled` property to `True` by default on `ReadOnlyPasswordHashField` in `django/contrib/auth/forms.py`. This makes the field properly use Django's built-in disabled field behavior which:

1. Ignores any user-submitted value in favor of the initial value
2. Marks the field as disabled at the Django forms level

The fix was a single line addition at `django/contrib/auth/forms.py:59`:
```python
kwargs.setdefault("disabled", True)
```

This ensures backward compatibility (using `setdefault` allows overriding if needed) while providing the safer default behavior. All existing tests pass with this change.

## Summary

The issue requested setting the `disabled` property to `True` by default on `ReadOnlyPasswordHashField` in `django/contrib/auth/forms.py`. This makes the field properly use Django's built-in disabled field behavior which:

1. Ignores any user-submitted value in favor of the initial value
2. Marks the field as disabled at the Django forms level

The fix was a single line addition at `django/contrib/auth/forms.py:59`:
```python
kwargs.setdefault("disabled", True)
```

This ensures backward compatibility (using `setdefault` allows overriding if needed) while providing the safer default behavior. All existing tests pass with this change.
